---
title: "Instructor Project Implementation"
description: "Synthetic-data release, submission, and checking workflow for approximately 60 students."
---

## Operating Assumptions

- Approximately 60 students form about 20 teams of three.
- Project 1 uses MATLAB; Project 2 uses R.
- Students receive instructor-generated data rather than finding or collecting
  data themselves.
- Each group receives a distinct synthetic building dataset with a common
  schema and comparable difficulty.
- The readable deliverable is PDF; executable source and results CSV files are
  submitted separately.
- Quarto and HTML are not required.
- Blackboard is used for group formation, file release, submission, and grades.
- Projects are group-assessed; individual competence is established through the
  quizzes, semester examination, and final examination.

Before creating the live releases, complete the
[laboratory and Blackboard readiness checklist](../resources/instructor-setup-checklist.qmd).

## Synthetic Building-Energy Data

The scenario is a real facilities-management problem represented by simulated
data. The student-facing materials must state clearly that the observations are
synthetic.

Each group represents a different building with its own simulated base load,
temperature sensitivity, operating effects, noise level, and unusual
observations. All datasets share variable names and units.

The private instructor package is generated locally under the Git-ignored
`instructor-private/project-data/` directory. It contains:

```text
generator/
  generate-project-data.R
  check-project-data.R
  assemble-project-packages.R
  check-project-packages.R
simulation-manifest.csv
quality-report.csv
student-packages/
  project-1/group-01/
  project-2-training/group-01/
  project-2-validation/group-01/
  zips/
checkers/
  check_project_1_submissions.m
  check-project-2-submissions.R
hidden/
  project-1-reference-results.csv
  project-2-data-issues.csv
  project-2-reference-results.csv
  project-2-reference-predictions.csv
release-project-1/
  group-01-matlab-data.csv
  group-01-project-1-assignment.csv
  ...
release-project-2-training/
  group-01-r-training.csv
  ...
release-project-2-validation/
  group-01-r-validation.csv
  ...
```

The package now generates 20 deterministic but distinct group assignments. The
generator, manifest, quality report, row-level truth, reference results, and
validation files must remain outside the public repository. The local package
must be backed up in an access-controlled location before the course begins.

The quality checker verifies schemas, row counts, identifiers, missingness,
allowed categories, plausible ranges, temperature coverage, model signal, and
comparable prediction difficulty. The current generated package passes all
checks for all 20 groups; file fingerprints were also confirmed to be distinct.

The package assembler creates 20 customized MATLAB starter ZIPs, 20 R training
starter ZIPs, and 20 separate validation ZIPs. The validation ZIPs must not be
released before the frozen model-plan deadline.

## Starter Materials

Every team receives the same scaffolded structure with filenames adjusted for
its group identifier.

For Project 1:

- partially completed main MATLAB script;
- a small function starter and function test;
- Word/Google Docs report template for PDF export;
- common data dictionary;
- assigned data file.

For Project 2:

- partially completed R script;
- Word/Google Docs report template for PDF export;
- common data dictionary;
- training file;
- later validation file.

## Week-Relative Milestones

The public [project milestone map](project-milestones.qmd) fixes the release
order while leaving exact calendar dates open.

| Course stage | Instructor action | Release source | Required control |
|---|---|---|---|
| Week 3 | Preview Project 1 and confirm groups | Public project pages and templates | Do not release group data as part of the preview |
| Week 4 | Release each Project 1 MATLAB ZIP | `release-project-1/` | Match ZIP and Blackboard Group identifier |
| Week 5 | Run the Project 1 readiness checkpoint | Already released files | Check data path, RMSE test, and one reproducible fit or figure; do not collect a second report |
| After Week 5 | Open the Project 1 Group Assignment | Blackboard | Exact deadline follows the Quiz 2 calendar decision |
| Weeks 9-10 | Preview Project 2 and confirm groups | Public project pages and templates | Explain the training/validation separation; do not release validation data |
| Week 12 | Release each Project 2 training ZIP | `release-project-2-training/` | Confirm that no validation outcome or file is present |
| After Week 13 | Collect one frozen model plan per group | Blackboard group checkpoint | Record the seven required plan fields before validation release |
| Week 14 | Release each Project 2 validation ZIP in one common window | `release-project-2-validation/` | Release only after the plan gate; do not give individual groups an early window |
| Week 15 | Open the final Project 2 Group Assignment and clean-run rehearsal | Blackboard and Week 15 materials | Exact deadline remains deferred; collect one group package |

The Project 1 completion window begins only after its Week 5 checkpoint. The
Project 2 validation gate is one-way: a later model change is documented as a
deviation or sensitivity analysis, not rewritten into the frozen plan.

### Blackboard Setup Checklist By Gate

- confirm the active group roster and group number before each package release;
- restrict every group-specific ZIP to the corresponding Blackboard Group;
- keep public previews separate from private data releases;
- use a short group checkpoint for the Project 2 plan, recording response,
  predictors, formula, primary coefficient, baseline, metric, and failure
  condition;
- release validation packages in one common window after the checkpoint closes;
- use one Blackboard Group Assignment per final project submission;
- require one group upload and ask all members to verify the receipt;
- download representative group 01, 10, and 20 files from the live course and
  compare filenames and ZIP contents with the private release manifest.

## Submission Intake

Create the teams as Blackboard Groups and use a Blackboard Group Assignment for
each project. Require fixed filenames and one ZIP file per team. A first-pass
checker should report missing files, unexpected filenames, unreadable PDFs, and
CSV schema errors before grading begins.

Release the group-specific data and starter files through Blackboard according
to the milestone map. Release Project 2 validation files in a common Week 14
window only after the frozen-model-plan checkpoint closes.

The final release contract has been rehearsed locally with all 60 ZIPs. An
exact allowlist check confirms the contents of every Project 1, Project 2
training, and Project 2 validation ZIP; the training ZIPs contain no validation
outcomes. Representative group 01, 10, and 20 ZIPs were also copied through an
upload/download staging cycle and extracted successfully. This rehearsal checks
the files and workflow contract; the live Blackboard course still requires a
short instructor setup check before student release.

## Automated Checking

### Project 1

Run every main MATLAB script in batch mode using its assigned dataset. Check:

- successful execution;
- required function behavior, including vector input;
- required figures or saved outputs;
- row counts and selected summaries;
- fitted coefficients and residual error;
- assigned prediction and sensitivity result;
- agreement with `project1-results.csv`.

### Project 2

Run every R script using its assigned training and validation files. Check:

- successful execution;
- row counts after cleaning;
- model formula and selected coefficients;
- baseline, training, and validation error metrics;
- one prediction per validation observation;
- agreement between predictions and the results CSV;
- sensitivity result.

The implemented checkers produce one instructor CSV row per group with file,
schema, execution, reproducibility, numerical-discrepancy, figure, and review
flags. Both checkers pass all 20 private reference submissions.

The Project 1 checker runs each MATLAB script in an isolated temporary folder,
tests `model_rmse.m` on row and column vectors, regenerates outputs, and compares
them with the hidden reference. The Project 2 checker runs each R script,
restricts the submitted formula to the approved variables and transformations,
independently refits it, and reproduces every result and validation prediction.

## PDF Review

Automated checks do not determine the whole grade. Review each PDF for:

- appropriate and readable figures;
- agreement between numbers, figures, and prose;
- correct mathematical or statistical interpretation;
- unsupported causal or extrapolative claims;
- meaningful limitations;
- quality of the AI-use appendix.

The instructor retains final responsibility for qualitative scores and grades.

## Project Verification Policy

There is no mandatory individual project examination. Each project is worth 10%
of the course, while quizzes and examinations provide 80% individual
assessment.

For each project, a small number of students may be selected randomly for a
five-to-ten-minute verification. A verification may also be requested when the
submitted files contain a material inconsistency or a contribution concern
requires clarification.

The student may be asked to explain a code fragment, interpret a result,
describe a contribution, or reproduce a small modification. Selection does not
imply suspected misconduct. A project–examination grade difference may inform a
review but is not sufficient evidence by itself.

If the first conversation leaves a serious unresolved concern, arrange a second
documented verification rather than applying an immediate penalty. Follow the
university's academic-integrity procedure if the concern remains.

The contribution statement and automated checks should resolve ordinary group-
work issues without requiring oral verification for all 60 students.

## Privacy and Repository Policy

- Use group identifiers rather than student names in data and checker outputs.
- Keep student submissions, grades, validation releases, generator parameters,
  and answer keys out of the public repository.
- Publish only student instructions, starter examples, and non-secret schemas.
